title: I watched a humanoid robot clean my apartment. It felt like a taste of the future.
gist: A hands-on review of Tau Robotics' San Francisco humanoid cleaning service, which is actually teleoperated by remote human pilots and priced low ($30-$100) because every cleaning generates training data for future autonomous models. The robots are slow, fragile to latency and infrastructure failures, and have done only a couple hundred cleanings, but already vacuum and mop autonomously and hint at labor displacement in cleaning and other physical jobs.
